It started off strong, but then got a boost with Covid, when folks had to switch to work-from-home … quickly. Today, they’re still growing an epic 60% (!) at almost $600m in ARR — although that’s down materially from the crazy rates during lockdowns (and perhaps not coincidentally, so is Zoom). Monday doesn’t break out its total customer count or even its paying customer base per se, but it does share that their logo churn rate remains low. Only 2.8% of logos left last quarter. That combined with 140+ NPS means most of us stay long-term. And also drives upsells. More on that below. #2. 130+ NPS Drives Logo Retention And Upsell s. While we don’t know exactly how many total customers Monday has (they only share paying ones), their net revenue retention isn’t quite 120%. The “Net” part of Net Revenue Retention is key. If your new customers pay less than existing customers do, your net revenue retention will be lower than 100%, no matter how fast your new bookings grow. This is true across multiple vendors I invest in and lead. So if Monday were truly growing 150% year-over-year, it would have a lot higher net NRR.

answer: How to Truly Stand Out in Any Job Interview, from SDR to COO The best candidates always stand out during interviews. Not because they’re arrogant or try too hard—it’s just that they’ve done their homework and are genuinely excited about what you do. Here’s how I’d approach it as an interviewee: First, Show Enthusiasm for What They Do Ask thoughtful questions like “What gets you most fired up about this company?” Don’t ask generic stuff like “What does the team work on?”—that shows you haven’t put any effort into understanding who they actually are. Instead, dig deeper. If they say something like “we’re building AI-powered tools,” your follow-up should be specific: “That sounds cool. Can you tell me more about how you see AI changing your industry?” This isn’t just small talk; it’s research. Second, Be Honest About Why You Want It Next, show them why you want the job specifically. For example, if you’re interviewing at a tech company but your background is in sales, don’t pretend you know everything about coding. Just be honest: “I’m not sure I could write code myself, but I love working with developers.” That shows humility and honesty. Third, Share Your Own Stories Finally, share stories from your own career where you overcame challenges similar to theirs. If they mention a tough project they worked on recently, think back to your own experiences. Did you once build a tool from scratch? Did you handle a difficult customer situation well?

answer: Your VCs Are Worried About Public Multiples. Do You Need To Worry, Too? So many founders I talk to are worried about how their VC will react if they don’t hit plan for next year. Or even worse, if growth slows down materially. They think the VCs are going to freak out. And maybe — sometimes that’s right. But my experience is most often … not so much. Why? First, it takes time. It may take your investors 12 months or more just to see this one slide, and realize things have changed. Second, it varies by fund size and type. Smaller funds especially, at least up until $100m-$200m+, need you to grow quickly enough to get them another check(s) back into the fund.
